### The Question of Questions
Author: Pastor Jeff Schreve
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/fromhisheart/from-his-heart-week-of-may-19-2017.html
Passage: John 5:6
Points:
- Jesus' inquiry cut straight to the core issue of whether the man genuinely desired a transformed life.
- People often become comfortable wallowing in misery and offering excuses rather than seeking change.
- Healing requires honest self-examination and confronting the reality of our condition before the Lord.
- Receiving God's transformative help demands humility, as pride prevents us from receiving grace.
- The Lord frequently provides healing and accountability through the support of fellow believers in the church.

### Do You Want to Get Well?
Author: Sharon Jaynes
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/girlfriends/do-you-want-to-get-well-girlfriends-in-god-december-3-2014.html
Passage: John 5:6, 8
Points:
- People can become so accustomed to emotional hurts that their wounds become a defining identity.
- Fixating on past trauma turns suffering into an idol that dictates our daily outlook and choices.
- Like the lame man, we often blame others and external circumstances instead of seeking freedom.
- Jesus commands believers to move beyond paralysis and take active steps into new life.
- God wants to use our past pain to propel us forward in faith rather than keep us captive.

### Healing at Bethesda
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier.org
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/healing-bethesda
Passage: John 5:1-9
Points:
- Jesus chose one invalid out of a large crowd, displaying His sovereign prerogative in dispensing mercy.
- Christ's miraculous work did not depend on the man's knowledge or the strength of his faith.
- Jesus' question addressed more than physical restoration, pointing toward a deeper need for spiritual renewal.
- As the sovereign Son of God, Jesus possesses authority that cannot be thwarted by any human limitation.
- Believers are encouraged to bring their needs in prayer, trusting God's power and timing.
